findings.what_happened: The PubMed query for my 'Sleep' topic is 'telemedicine OR sleep' AND 'Southeast Asia'; the OpenAlex one is 'telemedicine/telehealth' AND 'sleep' AND 'Southeast Asia'. Nothing about university students, grades or the UK appears. The page is titled 'Check the searches before they run', so I am invited to approve searches that plainly do not match what I typed.
findings.expected: Search blocks should reflect my answers (students, grades, UK). In demo mode, a note on this very step should say the searches are canned, not just a banner at the top.
findings.suggested_fix: In demo mode, label the query box 'Example search (demo): not built from your idea'. In real mode, assert that every group maps to a kept topic or scoping answer and warn if one does not.

findings.page: Step 9 Research question and Export report
findings.what_happened: All three candidate questions are about telemedicine in rural Southeast Asia ('What sleep factors shape telemedicine implementation in rural Southeast Asia?'). Candidate 2 reads 'What grades factors shape...'. The question has a '(mock)' prefix baked in. It is carried unchanged into the export header and report, so the report I would hand my tutor has a nonsense question and 'Population: Patients and providers', which contradicts my 'university students'.
findings.expected: The chosen question should be about my topic, or the exported file should be clearly stamped as a demo output that must not be handed in.
findings.suggested_fix: In demo mode, stamp the exported report with a visible 'DEMO: sample data, not a real review' banner in the first lines. Ideally let demo mode echo the user's own words.

findings.what_happened: The report intro says 'Every paper below comes from a database API record... AI-extracted claims carry verbatim quotes that were checked against the retrieved text.' It never says the papers are recorded samples unrelated to my topic, and it does not say some quotes were rejected or are unverified. The page-level demo banner does not travel with the downloaded file. It also leaks an internal id: 'Gap: ... [Lotfi et al. 2026, c_fda84bbbedb940fe]'.
findings.expected: A downloaded file is read on its own. It should carry the demo disclosure and human-readable citations only.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a demo-mode line to the report header and replace internal claim ids with the paper reference.

findings.what_happened: A paper I opened under Sleep (rank 2, 66/100, 'Enablers and Barriers of Telemedicine in Indonesia') shows 'Topic fit 1/5: 0 topic terms appear in title/abstract', yet it is auto-selected for a closer read. Rank 1 is a type 2 diabetes app trial. High design/recency scores outweigh zero topical relevance, and nothing warns that none of the selected papers mention sleep.
findings.expected: A paper with no topic match should not be pre-selected, or the page should warn 'none of the selected papers mention your topic'.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate selection on a minimum topic-fit score, and show a warning banner when the selected set has near-zero topic overlap.

findings.what_happened: Quotes labelled 'verified' do not answer the question they sit under. For example 'Clearly focused question: AI Unclear' is backed by the paper's title and first sentence, marked 'verified'. 'verified' only means the words exist in the text, not that they support the answer. A novice will read the green tick as 'the claim is true'.
findings.expected: Make clear that the tick means 'quote found in the paper', not 'claim confirmed'. Show quotes relevant to each question.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the badge 'quote found in text' and add a line 'Found means the words are in the paper, not that they prove the answer.'

findings.what_happened: After I rejected unverified quotes, the panel kept saying '11 unverified quotes to decide' and 'Decide every quote the check could not find (11 left)' and never ticked its checklist, while the canvas card dropped from 11 to 10 to 2 to 1. The rejected quote simply vanishes with no confirmation or undo. Paper 7 had two unverified quotes. 'Summarise the evidence' was allowed even though the card still said one unresolved. The paper list still labels papers '1 unverified' after rejecting, so I could not tell what was done.
findings.expected: Counters update immediately and agree everywhere. A rejected quote stays visible as 'Rejected' with Undo. Moving on warns if quotes remain undecided.
findings.suggested_fix: Drive all counters from one store, show rejected state in place with Undo, and block or confirm 'Summarise' when undecided quotes remain.

findings.what_happened: After clicking 'Appraise selected papers' the console reported a page error ('Failed to execute removeChild on Node'). The page kept showing the Step 6 content and the primary button vanished while the header said 'Now: step 7/9'. There was no progress or 'working' message. I waited ~10 s then had to reload and go back to the overview to find step 7. The same error appeared when moving from step 4 to 5, though that page recovered.
findings.expected: The page moves to step 7 or shows 'appraising, safe to close' progress, with no console error.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the 3D chart teardown (removeChild on an already-removed canvas). On run, show the running state with a spinner and auto-navigate to step 7 when done.

findings.what_happened: The page says 'Pick one; you can edit it' and 'then choose one; you can edit it after', but after 'Choose this question' I found no edit control. A student whose candidate is nonsense (all three were) has no visible way to fix it.
findings.expected: An 'Edit this question' field after choosing, or a way to write my own.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an inline 'Edit question' button on the chosen card, or remove the promise.

findings.what_happened: The 'Known' statement is just '(mock) 6 key findings were extracted for this topic.' and the conflict is '(mock) Placeholder contradiction... generated to demo highlighting', while its quote chips (e.g. a quote about technologies optimizing workflows) do not contradict anything. It is labelled mock, but it looks like a real 'conflict' card with green verified chips. Context and setting silently disappears from the topic tabs.
findings.expected: A synthesis statement says something specific, and a conflict shows two opposing quotes. Dropped topics should be explained.
findings.suggested_fix: In demo mode make placeholder conflicts visibly distinct (e.g. 'sample'). In real mode require each conflict to quote one claim per side. Say why a topic has no statements.

findings.what_happened: The topic 'Context and setting' shows '0 selected' and, when clicked, 'Showing all 0 ... No papers match these filters. Reset filters' although I set no filters. The checklist still says 'Keep 3-5 papers per topic', which is impossible here. I did not know whether I had broken something.
findings.expected: A message such as 'No papers were matched to this topic. Remove the topic or add a search' with a link back to step 2 or 3.
findings.suggested_fix: Special-case an empty topic with an explanation and actions, and warn before appraisal if a topic has no papers.

findings.what_happened: The canvas card shows '10 papers' though 12 papers were selected in step 6, with no explanation. The card badge '✓ 94 ✕ 11' has no label (the list view labels it '94 verified'), and I did not know what the numbers counted.
findings.expected: Explain why 2 papers dropped out, and label the badge ('94 quotes found, 11 not found').
findings.suggested_fix: Add text labels to the badge and a 'why 10 of 12' note.

findings.page: Step 5 Summary table and Step 6 Ranking
findings.what_happened: Choosing 'Trial' and 'Review article' filters together gives 'Showing 0 of 115: trial; review article', since groups combine with AND. The chip counts (5 and 14) suggest I would see 19.
findings.expected: Say that different groups narrow each other (study type AND article type). Show live counts or disable chips that would give zero.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a hint under the chips ('Choosing from both rows shows papers matching both') and update chip counts to match the other filter.

findings.page: Retrieval, Summary table, Ranking (categories and colours)
findings.what_happened: The study-type colours, shapes and legend are clear, clicking a legend item isolates it, and the 'Showing X of Y' wording is honest. But on the retrieval page I could not filter article type at all (only a bar chart), and the 'Colour by' menu has no Article type, so the article-type view lives only in the table. In the first chart the legend label 'Systematic / scoping revi...' is cut off. The 3D chart is small, the year axis shows only '2026' and 'Height has no meaning yet', so it adds little for a first-time user.
findings.expected: I can find papers by article type and study type at every list. Axis ticks and labels are readable.
findings.suggested_fix: Show the article-type chips on the retrieval page as well, add year ticks, widen the legend label.

findings.what_happened: The password hint ('At least 10 characters, not containing the name part of your email.') is drawn on top of the bottom of the password input box, so the box looks cut and the hint overlaps its border. The helper also reported the Create account button as 'looks disabled' while it was an enabled blue button.
findings.expected: The hint sits below the field without overlap.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the hint its own line below the input (margin or grid row).

findings.what_happened: After I typed my idea on /s/new, the canvas shows a card 'Tell us what you want to research' with 'Open step 1' and 'Sharpen my idea' (two buttons for the same thing), then step 1 asks for the same idea again. The scoping questions then double up: one answer fills both 'Who' and 'Where', and 'years' and 'kinds of studies' got the same text. The counter says '3 of 5 questions' after four answers, and the panel says '3 questions' while 'What we know so far' says '6 of 6 answered'.
findings.expected: One obvious next action, and answers mapped to the right fields. Counters that agree.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip step 1 if the idea was already entered, or prefill it with a single 'Continue'. Ask one thing per question.

findings.what_happened: After approving, the panel stays on the previous node (e.g. 'Viewing step 2 of 9 - Edit this search topic' while the strip says step 3) and shows a 'Go to step 2: Scoping' or 'Go to step 4: Retrieval' button; I had to click through before I saw the real next step. The word 'Query' and 'PubMed - OpenAlex -' show dashes for four of the queries after retrieval has finished.
findings.expected: After I approve, the panel moves to the next step automatically. Dashes should say 'not counted'.
findings.suggested_fix: Auto-open the next step panel on approval and replace dashes with 'not counted'.

findings.what_happened: The report is a Markdown file described as 'opens in Word, Google Docs or any text editor'. A first-year will open it in Word and see raw # symbols. After clicking Download there was no visible confirmation. The preview shows only 200 of 664 lines in a small scroll box, and the appraisal and synthesis sections cannot be seen before downloading.
findings.expected: A .docx or PDF option, or honest wording about what Word will show, and a 'Downloaded' confirmation.
findings.suggested_fix: Offer Word or PDF, change the copy to 'plain text with simple formatting', and show a toast on download.

findings.what_happened: The 'What happens in this step - 8 s' row is cryptic: I read '8 s' as 8 seconds of what. Jargon appears undefined at first sight: '0 MeSH' on topic cards, 'PICo' and 'PECO' on candidates, 'index term', 'Controlled vocabulary'. MeSH is explained only inside the topic editor.
findings.expected: '8 s' becomes 'Watch a 8-second preview'. Jargon gets a one-line plain explanation or a tooltip where it first appears.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the row, and add tooltips for MeSH, PICo and PECO.

findings.what_happened: On the table pages, the left link 'Overview' did not seem to take me anywhere (the URL stayed on /table after I clicked it); I got to the overview only by opening the project address directly. The checklist box sits to the right of a large empty gap under the title on desktop.
findings.expected: Overview opens the canvas for the review.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the Overview link target on the table route, and rebalance the header layout.

three_second_test.note: Understood: a tool that turns a rough idea into a research question backed by real papers. First: click 'Start a review'. Next: sign up. The headline, 9-step and 3-stage cards and the 'what Athena will not do' box are reassuring. It does not say up front that this is a demo, and the auto-playing demo shows a health-systems example.
Create an account with name, email and password, then press Create account. Standard, but the password hint overlaps the box.
Type my idea in a box, click 'Start my review'. The example chips and 'Next: up to five short questions' make it feel safe.

I saw a dark dotted canvas with one card and a demo banner. I guessed it showed my idea and that I should click 'Open step 1', but 'Sharpen my idea' on the card did the same thing and I was unsure which to pick. The step strip with numbers 1-9 helped.
Answer the question in the box and click Send answer. 'Skip the rest' is visible. The side summary ('What we know so far') is clear.
Keep or delete the suggested topics, then press 'Keep 4 suggested topics'. The topic names ('Measurement and outcomes') felt vague, though.

I understood I should check the searches and press 'Run all 8 searches', but the groups (telemedicine, Southeast Asia) made no sense for sleep and grades, and AND/any-of logic is hard for a beginner. I did not know whether to edit or trust it.
See how many papers were found (115, 50 duplicates removed) and press 'Summarise the papers'. The 'What kinds of papers you are getting' bars and the legend are easy to read.

A table of papers with filter chips for study type and article type; the 'Do these 3 things' checklist told me what to do; 'Rank the papers' is the next step. The chart colours and shapes are readable from the legend.
Pick a topic, check the selected papers, press 'Appraise selected papers'. The 'How papers are scored' box is very reassuring, though one topic had zero papers and I was not told why.
Go paper by paper, decide on quotes marked unverified, then 'Summarise the evidence'. The checklist is clear, but the stale counters ('11 left') were confusing.
Read known, contested and unknown for each topic, then press 'Suggest research questions'. The content itself is placeholder text.

Compare three candidates and click 'Choose this question', then 'Finish and export'. Gap, feasibility and weakness per card are good, and the novelty caveat is there, but the question text itself is nonsense for my topic.
'Your literature review is ready': pick a format and download. Three format cards and the preview make it clear.

reports.categories_and_colours: I could find and filter by both study type and article type, but in different places. Step 5 and 6 tables have two rows of filter chips with counts: study type (Trial, Cohort / case-control, Cross-sectional, Qualitative / mixed methods, Systematic / scoping review, Other design, Not reported) and article type (Journal article, Review article, Preprint, Editorial / letter / comment). On the retrieval page there are bar charts for both, but I could only filter by study type via the chart legend; the 'Colour by' menu offers Study type, Topic, Source database (and Ranking score on the ranking step), not Article type. The study-type legend uses colour plus shape: blue circle = Trial, orange square = Cohort / case-control, green triangle = Cross-sectional, amber diamond = Qualitative / mixed methods, pink star = Systematic / scoping review, green cross = Other design, grey ring = Not reported. I understood them without being told, because each legend entry has a label and a shape, and clicking one showed only that category ('Showing only one category (5 papers). Click it again to show all.'). Counts add up (retrieval: 5+2+9+99 = 115; table: 5+2+18+20+9+42+19 = 115; article types 85+14+6+10 = 115). The counts change between retrieval (99 not reported) and the table (19 not reported) because the AI reads the abstracts, which the page says. Misleading bits: 'Other design' (cross) and 'Cross-sectional' (triangle) are both green and easy to confuse; the 3D chart is small, depth means topic and height means nothing; combining a study-type chip with an article-type chip gives 0 results without explanation; the legend label 'Systematic / scoping revi...' is truncated on the retrieval page.
reports.validity_assessment: The workflow design is trustworthy: demo mode is announced in a dismissible banner, AI text is marked '(mock)', every quote is checked word for word, unverified quotes are flagged red with the closest passage shown, rankings show a transparent score breakdown, abstract-only versus full text is stated per paper, and the novelty check carries the caveat that finding none does not prove novelty. Weaknesses: (1) in demo mode the searches, the 115 papers, the synthesis and all three candidate questions are about telemedicine in Southeast Asia, so the final 'review' is unusable for sleep and grades, and the '(mock)' prefix stays in the exported question; (2) the exported report does not repeat the demo disclosure, and its header sentence 'Every paper below comes from a database API record... quotes were checked' reads as a real assurance; (3) 'verified' means the quote exists, not that it supports the answer; (4) papers with no topic match (Topic fit 1/5, 0 terms) are still pre-selected; (5) the synthesis conflict is an invented 'placeholder contradiction'. I did not see anything fabricated beyond the clearly labelled mock content, and the one deliberately altered quote was caught and flagged. For a real run I could trace statements to papers via the chip popovers (quote text, 'Open paper'), DOIs and PMIDs in the report.
reports.would_have_quit_at: Step 3 (Search builder), when the searches for my 'Sleep' topic were about telemedicine in Southeast Asia and I had no idea whether I should fix them. The demo banner kept me going. A real student would very likely stop at step 9 on seeing 'What sleep factors shape telemedicine implementation in rural Southeast Asia?', with no way to edit it, or at step 6 where papers with zero topic match were pre-selected.
reports.activity: Created one account (mai.undergrad.qa@example.com, name Mai) and one project, 'I'm interested in sleep and grades' (prj_5d910500288d4f6a). Answered 4 scoping questions, kept all 4 AI-suggested topics, counted one PubMed query (979 matches) and ran all 8 searches (165 results, 50 duplicates removed, 115 papers). Summarised 115 papers (12/12 batches), tried study- and article-type filters (including a 0-result combination), ranked and appraised 12 selected papers (10 appraised, 4 full text). Rejected about 10 unverified quotes (11 flagged) and left roughly one undecided, ran the synthesis (9 statements, 3 placeholder conflicts), chose candidate 1 of 3 research questions and reached the export page; opened the larger preview and clicked 'Download the report (Markdown)' (no visible confirmation, so I could not verify the file). Also viewed the List view and checked keyboard focus once. Errors seen: a console page error 'Failed to execute removeChild on Node' when summarising papers (step 4 to 5) and when starting appraisal (step 6 to 7); no failed network requests. About 115 helper commands used. Browser stopped at the end.
reports.narrative: I felt reassured on the landing page: plain headline, nine steps, and a clear list of what Athena will not do. Sign-up was easy, though the password hint sat on top of the box. I typed my vague idea, and the demo banner told me straight away that papers would be about telemedicine, which stopped me panicking later. Scoping questions were friendly and let me say I was not sure about years. The topics were vague ('Measurement and outcomes'), and at step 3 the searches talked about telemedicine and Southeast Asia, which made no sense to me, so I trusted the banner and pressed on. Retrieval was my favourite part: 165 results, 50 duplicates, 115 papers, and shapes plus labels I could understand. The table checklist told me exactly what to do. The ranking page's score breakdown felt honest, but it showed a paper with zero topic match being selected, and one topic had no papers with a confusing 'No papers match these filters' message. After I clicked 'Appraise selected papers' the page just sat there on step 6; I only found step 7 by reloading. In appraisal, the red flagged quote with its closest passage was a great feature, but counters kept saying 11 left after I rejected things, and green 'verified' ticks on irrelevant quotes confused me. The synthesis felt empty. The three questions were all about telemedicine, I could not edit mine, and the report I would show my tutor says '(mock)' in the question. I was proud of finishing but I could not hand it in.

reports.would_have_quit_at: I would not have quit in the flow itself (it is navigable and I reached export in about 45 commands). I would have quit at the research-question step, and after that the exported report: the "question" is about telemedicine in rural Southeast Asia, nothing to do with ICU nurses, and the "(mock)" prefix is baked into it. Demo-mode caveat: a real run might not have this problem, but the flow would still let me skip quote checks and papers per topic without warning. The first moment I truly lost trust was the search-builder page, where my ICU nurse topic produced searches for telemedicine in Thailand and Vietnam. I would then have asked whether any of this was real.
reports.activity: Created account daniel.masters.qa@example.com (first attempt rejected for an 8-character password, second succeeded). Created one project (prj_6dd16e1541804a53) with the idea "Effect of mindfulness-based interventions on burnout in ICU nurses". Answered 2 of up to 5 scoping questions, then skipped the rest. Kept 6 suggested topics and clicked "Use these topics". Ran the 12 searches (PubMed and OpenAlex), got 205 fetched, 78 duplicates, 127 papers. Summarised the papers, filtered the table by Trial, reset filters, ranked (16 selected, Burnout and Context and setting at 0), and ran appraisal (11 papers, 117 quotes found, 12 not found, none decided by me). Summarised the evidence, got 3 candidate questions, chose candidate 1, finished and clicked Download Markdown (no visible confirmation), and opened the larger preview. Errors seen: a 400 console error right after signup, and a page error "removeChild ... not a child of this node" on arriving at the step 5 summary table. No other failed requests. Screenshots 01 to 41 are in docs/qa/iteration-1/masters/. Browser stopped.
reports.categories_and_colours: Study type: Trial (blue circle), Cohort/case-control (orange square), Cross-sectional (green triangle), Qualitative/mixed methods (amber diamond), Systematic/scoping review (pink star), Other design (green cross), Not reported (grey ring). Article type (Journal article, Review article, Preprint, Editorial/letter/comment) is a separate row of plain chips with no colour. I could find and filter papers by both study type and article type, in the step 4 retrieval summary (bars plus 3D chart) and in the step 5/6 table. Each chip has a colour, a shape and a count, and clicking one filters. The page says "Showing 4 of 127: trial. 123 papers are hidden by your filters (still in the review)" and Reset filters stays visible, which is honest. I understood the encoding without being told: colour and shape equal study type and the legend lists it. Problems: (1) the step 4 legend lists Cohort, Cross-sectional and Qualitative with no count (dimmed), while the bars show only 4 labelled types, which is ambiguous. (2) the 3D chart is small and mostly grey circles, "Height has no meaning yet", and the caption keeps saying "127 papers" when only 4 dots are filtered. (3) two different "greens" (cross-sectional triangle and other-design cross) are told apart only by shape. (4) "Colour by Topic" works but the topics are junk. (5) Protocols are classed as "Trial / Randomised trial", which is misleading as study evidence (see findings). (6) "Other design" mixes narrative reviews with other things, while "Review article" appears under the article type, so a user may wonder why the same paper is in both.
reports.validity_assessment: Honesty is mostly good: a persistent demo banner, "(mock)" tags on AI text, a novelty-check caveat ("Finding none does not prove a question is new"), filters described as views and not deletions, a transparent 5-criterion score rubric under "Why this score", and quote chips that link statements to papers (e.g. "Rumi et al. 2026 · limitation"). Weaknesses for a real review: (1) The review is not grounded in my topic, because demo data is telemedicine in Southeast Asia, and the searches, scoring and candidate questions all reflect that. The banner says so, but the exported report has only an intro line saying quotes "were checked", with no demo disclaimer, so a rushed student could paste a "(mock)" telemedicine question into a proposal. (2) "Verified" means only that a string occurs in the text, not that it supports the answer: the first "verified" quote for "Random allocation method described: Unclear" is just the paper title. (3) The user can proceed to synthesis, question and export with 12 undecided "not found" quotes and with 0 papers selected for two topics, no warning, and the report header still claims claims were checked. (4) The synthesis is placeholder text ("7 key findings were extracted", "Placeholder contradiction...") but carries green verified ticks; this is labelled mock, but in a real run the ticks on a placeholder would mislead. (5) Trial protocols are labelled "Trial / Randomised trial" and their "key finding" is a registration number, which is not evidence. (6) The novelty check reports 8,058 PubMed hits for a very narrow query whose top hits are unrelated; with real data this would be a strong signal against novelty, but the page does not interpret it. (7) Answers I gave in scoping were not used (topics ignore nurses, Maslach Burnout Inventory) and "What we know so far" reverts to "not answered yet". (8) The preview shows raw internal IDs in citations. Nothing looked fabricated beyond the clearly labelled mock text, and every paper has a DOI/PMID. For a real dissertation I could not yet trust the pipeline end to end, but the design intent (verbatim quotes, visible rubric, caveats) is sound.

three_second_test.note: What for: turn a rough idea into a research question backed by real papers. First: click Start a review. Next: sign up. Clear headline and two buttons. The three illustrated cards are decorative to an impatient user.

What for: create an account. First: email and password. Next: Create account. Clear, but the password hint is drawn on top of the password input (overlaps), so I missed the 10-character rule and had to retry.
What for: type my idea. First: type or click an example. Next: Start my review. Very clear, with a helpful 'Next:' line.

I saw one card, a long demo banner, and two competing actions ('Open step 1' and 'Sharpen my idea'). I guessed Open step 1. A canvas with a single node and an empty field means nothing to a first-timer, and it asks 'Tell us what you want to research' when I already typed it.

I read it as 'check each paper and decide on quotes'. The canvas card shows ✓117 ✗12 with no label. Long checklist, 'AI: Unclear', 'verified', 'Pin to canvas' and 'Abstract only' all appear before the main action.

reports.narrative: I arrived as Daniel with two days to go, clicked Start a review, signed up (my first password was too short because the hint is drawn on top of the field), and typed my topic. Then the app asked me again for the same idea on a second page, plus a canvas with one lonely card, and two buttons with different names for the same thing. I answered two scoping questions, skipped the rest, and the summary then said 'not answered yet' for everything I had just said. The suggested topics had nothing about nurses. I kept them all (two clicks for one decision) and then saw the searches mention telemedicine, Thailand and Vietnam. The demo banner had warned me, but it still made me doubt the app. Retrieval was the clearest page: 205 fetched, 78 duplicates, 127 left, with study types and article types shown separately in colour, shape and count, and filters worked and said how many were hidden. After I clicked Appraise there was no progress at all, only the top bar changing. The appraisal page promised word-for-word checked quotes, but the first 'verified' quote was just the paper title, and I was allowed to skip 12 unverified quotes and papers for two topics with no warning. The synthesis was clearly placeholder. The three research questions were grammatically broken telemedicine questions with '(mock)' in the text. I picked one, found Finish and export, and the report preview looked professional but showed raw IDs in citations, and Download gave no feedback. I did get to the end quickly, but I would not trust the result for my dissertation.

findings.what_happened: I answered two scoping questions (nurses in adult ICUs; Maslach Burnout Inventory), then clicked Skip the rest. The 'What we know so far' panel then showed 'not answered yet' for Who, Where, What is studied and 'What you want to know', and later said '0 of 6 answered'. The suggested topics ignored my answers: Mindfulness-based, Interventions, Burnout, Icu, Measurement and outcomes, Context and setting. Nothing about nurses.
findings.expected: My answers appear in the summary and shape the topics; skipping the rest should keep what I already said.
findings.suggested_fix: Persist and show answered fields after skipping; feed answers into topic suggestions; if the scripted demo cannot do that, say so in the panel rather than showing 'not answered yet'.

findings.what_happened: After clicking Appraise selected papers the button vanished, the top bar changed to 'step 7/9 · Appraisal', but the page content stayed on step 6 with the same checklist (0 of 3 done). reports.validity_assessment:
TRACEABILITY IS STRONG. The search syntax is visible and editable (PubMed [mh]/[tiab] and OpenAlex boolean text), with "Reset to AI version". There is a per-query table of hits, fetched, new and total, and a per-query cap of 40 is disclosed. Every paper carries a DOI/PMID. The 5-criterion scoring rubric is explained per paper, and "Why this score" shows each criterion. Swaps and edits are labelled "changed by you" / "edited by you". Full text versus abstract-only is marked on every appraisal. "Show source" highlights the quote in context. The app planted a deliberately altered quote ("clearly proves the intervention works everywhere"), flagged it as unverified, and made me accept or reject it. I rejected all of them, and the report shows 139 verified and 14 not. The novelty check shows its queries and counts and says "Finding none does not prove a question is new". The app does not overclaim novelty. Demo mode is announced at the top of every page, and AI text carries "(mock)".

METHODOLOGICAL AND HONESTY PROBLEMS:
1. In demo mode the outputs ignored my inputs and nothing at the point of use said so. Generated queries dropped my MeSH term and substituted telemedicine plus Southeast Asia. Dates 2020 to now were not applied: the selected set includes a 2019 paper, and the synthesis cites Lee 2015 and Clough 2019. My rewritten inclusion/exclusion criteria did not affect scoring, which rewards "Mentions a Southeast Asian setting". The final research question is about telemedicine in rural Southeast Asia. The banner explains this globally, but the exported report does not mention demo mode or the sample-paper caveat at the top.
2. Match counts are not credible. The same edited PubMed query showed 183 matches, then 9,245 after I only moved the start year later, which cannot be right. The 183 reappeared as the count for a different topic's query. The counts look keyed to the query slot, not the query text.
3. Advice that is wrong for a systematic review. "9,245 papers match. Broad: only the 40 most relevant are collected, so that is fine" tells a reviewer that truncating 9,245 records to 40 is fine. There is no PRISMA-style flow of identified, screened, eligible and included, no title/abstract screening stage, and no dual screening. Papers are selected by an AI score plus "top 3 to 5 per topic", not by eligibility criteria.
4. The ranking does not flag irrelevance. The top Long COVID paper scored 54/100 although its own breakdown says "Topic fit 1/5: 0 topic terms appear in title/abstract", and it was still pre-selected. Zero hits across all my long-COVID papers triggered no "no relevant papers found" warning.
5. "Verified" is overstated. The check confirms that the quote exists in the text, not that it supports the answer. "Aim clearly stated: AI Unclear" is backed by a verified quote that is just the paper title. The report header says "AI-extracted claims carry verbatim quotes that were checked against the retrieved text", which reads as if the claims were checked too. A synthesis "contradiction" is a placeholder with green verified chips, and its quote is a background sentence, not a finding.
6. The AI summary table has obvious extraction errors, for example a "key finding" that is just a postal address ("Sutami 36A, Surakarta 57126, Central Java, Indonesia"). The rubric includes citation impact, which penalises new long-COVID literature, and the missing-citation case scores 0/5.
7. The report is partly invalid as a deliverable. Its OpenAlex queries for other topics contain an empty group, `AND () AND`. The Long COVID topic rationale still reads "(mock) Key concept from your idea: association" after I renamed the topic. The research question cannot be edited, although the page says "you can edit it".

VERDICT: the traceability machinery is the right shape and would help a real reviewer. In this run the content was off-topic and partly invalid, and the app does not warn when topic fit is zero. As a rigorous review it is not defensible: it is a good scaffold for reasoning, not a methodologically sound review.
reports.narrative: I arrived sceptical. The landing page told me within a few seconds what Athena is for and offered "Start a review". After signing up I typed my topic and answered Athena's scoping questions in detail. The first thing I noticed was that "long" and "covid" were split into two separate topics, which a methodologist would never do. I could rescue that by editing a topic, adding my own synonyms and a MeSH term, deleting the others and adding two topics. I liked that. The search builder showed the real PubMed and OpenAlex syntax and let me rewrite it, which is exactly what I wanted. Then I noticed the generated queries contained telemedicine and Southeast Asia and had dropped my MeSH term. The demo banner explained this, but it meant I could not test whether my edits would have been honoured in a real run. I rewrote the queries and the criteria, and I lost a first edit of the criteria silently because it needed a separate Save. The counts jumped from 183 to 9,245 for a narrower query, and the app said 9,245 records truncated to 40 was "fine". I did not believe either. The colour and shape key, the filters and the "hidden by your filters" warning were clear and honest. I swapped a paper and opened the score breakdown. The top paper had zero topic terms and was still selected. In appraisal I was impressed that a fabricated quote was flagged and that "Show source" highlighted the quote in context. But "verified" only means the quote exists. Synthesis contained placeholder contradictions. The three research questions were about telemedicine in Southeast Asia, I could not find where to edit the chosen question, and the report preview mixed my edits with stale mock text. I would not defend this to my committee, but the audit trail is the most promising part.

findings.what_happened: The generated PubMed and OpenAlex queries ignored my edited topic. My MeSH term 'Post-Acute COVID-19 Syndrome' was replaced by 'telemedicine[mh]', and a Southeast Asia block was added. Years default to 2015 to now, not the 2020 I asked for. The inclusion and exclusion criteria were pre-filled with Southeast Asian telemedicine text. Only a '(mock)' label in small text hints at this.
findings.expected: Queries that reflect my topic's synonyms and MeSH terms, and criteria derived from my scoping answers, or an explicit statement at the point of use that demo mode does not use my input.
findings.suggested_fix: When demo mode is on, put a visible banner on the query panel itself ('these queries are scripted and do not use your topics'). In real mode, build the query from the topic's synonyms and MeSH and never overwrite user-entered MeSH.

findings.what_happened: Match counts look arbitrary. The same PubMed query showed 183 matches and then 9,245 after I only moved the start year later. A different topic's query later showed the same 183. The app also said 9,245 records truncated to 40 'is fine'.
findings.expected: Narrowing a query can never increase the count. A count must come from the query text, or be clearly marked as simulated. Truncating thousands of records to 40 should be a warning, not 'fine'.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark simulated counts as sample numbers next to the count. Replace 'so that is fine' with a warning that a systematic review needs the full result set or a justified cap. Let the user raise the cap.

findings.what_happened: The top-ranked, pre-selected paper for my Long COVID topic scored 54/100 although its own breakdown says 'Topic fit 1/5: 0 topic terms appear in title/abstract'. Every selected paper was off-topic (telemedicine, stroke, diabetes). The app forces 3 to 5 papers per topic and gave no warning that nothing matched. Setting match rewarded 'Mentions a Southeast Asian setting', not my criteria.
findings.expected: A warning when the best paper has near-zero topic fit, a minimum relevance threshold, and scoring that uses the criteria I entered.
findings.suggested_fix: Show a banner when the top paper for a topic has topic fit of 1/5 or less ('none of these papers appear to match this topic'). Allow selecting fewer than 3 papers or none. Feed saved criteria into the Setting match criterion.

findings.what_happened: 'Verified' means only that the quote text exists in the source, not that it supports the answer. 'Aim clearly stated: AI Unclear' is backed by a verified quote that is just the paper title. A synthesis 'contradiction' that is plainly a placeholder carries green verified chips. The report header says 'AI-extracted claims carry verbatim quotes that were checked', which reads as claim-level assurance.
findings.expected: A distinction between 'quote found in text' and 'quote supports the claim', and wording that does not imply the claim itself was validated.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the badge to 'quote found in source'. Add a user control 'quote supports this answer: yes/no'. Reword the report header to say that only the existence of quotes was checked, not their interpretation.

findings.what_happened: The three candidate questions and the final report are about telemedicine in rural Southeast Asia. Candidate 2 is labelled 'effect of an exposure' with a PECO structure but is not an effect question. All three share the same one-line feasibility and weakness. The exported report has no demo-mode or off-topic caveat at the top. The page says 'you can edit it', but I could not find any way to edit the chosen question.
findings.expected: A question related to my idea, or a clear caveat in the export that this review used sample data. A working edit control after choosing.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an 'Edit question' field on the chosen card. Add a prominent demo-data line at the top of the report when demo mode is on.

findings.what_happened: The other topics' generated OpenAlex queries contain an empty group, for example `("telemedicine" OR "telehealth") AND () AND ("Southeast Asia"...)`. This is invalid boolean syntax and would fail or return garbage in a real search. The 'Healthcare workers' and 'Work ability' topics, which have no synonyms, produced it. The Long COVID topic's rationale still reads '(mock) Key concept from your idea: association' after I renamed the topic.
findings.expected: No empty groups. A topic with no synonyms should fall back to its own name. Rationale text should update, or be cleared, when I edit a topic.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate generated queries before display and omit empty groups. Seed a topic with its own name as a synonym. Clear or regenerate the rationale on edit.

findings.what_happened: The year filter I set to 2020 and saved did not stop 2015 and 2019 papers appearing. 'Going global' (2019) was selected and 'Lee et al. 2015' and 'Clough et al. 2019' are cited in the synthesis. This is demo data, but nothing says dates were not applied.
findings.expected: Date limits applied, or a visible statement that recorded sample papers ignore them.
findings.suggested_fix: Filter by year after retrieval as a safety net, or show 'dates not applied in demo mode'.

findings.what_happened: There is no PRISMA-style flow and no title/abstract screening step. Selection is an AI score plus 'top 3 to 5 per topic'. No eligibility decision is recorded per paper and no second reviewer is possible. The only deduplication information is '24 duplicates merged'. The per-query cap of 40 is disclosed but the effect on completeness is not discussed.
findings.expected: For a review I would defend: identified, screened, excluded-with-reason and included counts, per-paper inclusion or exclusion with a reason, and an explicit statement that this is a rapid scoping exercise and not a systematic review.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a flow diagram to the report. Add an include/exclude with reason column. Label the output as a 'guided rapid review' unless full screening exists.

findings.what_happened: I typed new inclusion and exclusion criteria, clicked 'Count matches', and my text silently reverted to the mock text. A separate Save criteria button had appeared lower down, below the fold. Another place on the same page says 'Changes save when you leave a field'. I lost my first edit.
findings.expected: Edits saved on blur, or a clear unsaved-changes warning before anything discards them.
findings.suggested_fix: Autosave on blur like the other fields, or disable other actions and show 'unsaved changes' until Save or Undo.

findings.what_happened: After I rejected all 14 unverified quotes the canvas count went from 14 to 0, but the panel text still read '14 left' in the checklist and '14 unverified quotes to decide' under the paper header. The last paper (15 of 15) could not be marked reviewed: 'Next paper' was disabled, so the counter stayed at 14/15 reviewed.
findings.expected: Counters that update, and a way to mark the final paper as reviewed.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the counters from current decisions. On the last paper, change the button to 'Mark reviewed'.

findings.what_happened: After clicking 'Appraise selected papers' the header said 'Now: step 7/9 Appraisal' but the page still showed the step 6 table and checklist. The primary button disappeared and there was no progress or confirmation. I only found the result by going back to Overview.
findings.expected: A progress state or automatic navigation to the appraisal step.
findings.suggested_fix: Show 'Appraising 15 papers...' with progress and then navigate, or keep a visible 'Go to step 7' button.

findings.what_happened: My search text 'Meta-Analysis' from step 5 carried over into the ranking step and showed '1 of 111'. A 'Keep 3 to 5 papers per topic' item was already ticked on arrival.
findings.expected: Filters reset between steps, or a visible reminder. Checklist items that are ticked only when I do them.
findings.suggested_fix: Reset the search and filters when the step changes. Mark the checklist item only after the user has seen the selection.

findings.what_happened: The browser reported a page error: "Failed to execute 'removeChild' on 'Node': The node to be removed is not a child of this node." It appeared when the app moved to step 5 and left the 3D papers view. The page kept working.
findings.expected: No console errors.

findings.what_happened: The first canvas screen has a single Idea node marked 'Your turn' while the step strip already shows step 1 as 'Approved'. Two buttons compete: 'Open step 1' and 'Sharpen my idea'. The top card says 'Tell us what you want to research' although I had already typed it.
findings.expected: One obvious next action, and wording that reflects what I already did.
findings.suggested_fix: After the idea is entered, say 'Next: answer a few questions' and offer one button. Mark step 1 done.

findings.what_happened: The scoping answers shown under 'What we know so far' are truncated to roughly 80 characters ('allied health) wi', 'sustained employment at'). Two separate questions copied my single combined answer into both 'Which years' and 'Which kinds of studies'. 'Where' stayed 'not answered yet' although I had said 'any country'.
findings.expected: Full answers, or a clear ellipsis. Answers mapped to the right fields.
findings.suggested_fix: Show full text with an expand toggle, and add an ellipsis. Parse answers per question.

findings.what_happened: The AI suggested 'Association', 'Long' and 'Covid' as separate search topics, splitting the phrase 'long COVID'. 'Long' alone as a search topic would return noise. The topic list also showed a 'Context and setting' topic, which disappeared when I clicked its name.
findings.expected: Multi-word concepts kept together, and clicking a name should not delete it.
findings.suggested_fix: Tokenise on concepts (noun phrases) instead of single words. Check why clicking the topic name removed it, and add Undo on Delete.

findings.what_happened: After I edited a suggested topic, its state became 'Your turn' with no Keep or Delete. The only button was 'Go to step 2: Scoping' while I was already on step 2. It was unclear whether the topic was accepted. Deleting topics happened instantly with no confirmation or undo.
findings.expected: A clear accepted state, a sensible button label, and a way to undo a delete.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep 'Keep this topic' visible after editing. Show an 'Undo' toast on delete.

findings.what_happened: AI-drafted 'key finding' cells included clearly wrong extracts, such as a postal address and a background sentence. After I edited the key finding, an 'edited by you' badge also appeared under Study type, which I had not changed. Pressing Enter in the edit box did not commit (Tab did), and the hint did not say so.
findings.expected: A badge only on the cell I edited, a hint about how to save, and extractions that give a result.
findings.suggested_fix: Show the badge per cell. Add 'Press Tab or click away to save, Esc to cancel'. Flag key findings that look like addresses or boilerplate.

findings.what_happened: After the run the per-topic query cards still read 'PubMed – OpenAlex –' for four of the five queries, although the search table below shows hits for them. The 'Colour by' menu had no Article type, evidence status or score option, although I was asked to filter by article type.
findings.expected: Counts on the query cards after a run, and article type available as a view.
findings.suggested_fix: Refresh the query cards with run counts. Add Article type as a colour-by or group-by option in the 3D and 2D views.

findings.what_happened: The PubMed and OpenAlex query textareas have no accessible name. When focused, the focus helper reported an empty name, and the helper could not find them by their visible labels 'PubMed' and 'OpenAlex'. A screen-reader user would hear only 'edit text'.
findings.expected: Each textarea labelled 'PubMed search text' and 'OpenAlex search text'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a label or aria-labelledby to each textarea, tied to the visible 'PubMed' and 'OpenAlex' headings.

findings.what_happened: The report preview sits in a small inner scroll box (about 12 lines tall). It is hard to read a 914-line report and to find the search strategy or limitations. The panel metric 'Quotes verified / not: 139 / 14' does not say that I rejected the 14.
findings.expected: A full-height preview or a table of contents, and a count of how many unverified quotes I rejected.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the preview taller with a section index, and show 'unverified: 14 (rejected by you)'.

findings.what_happened: The password hint ('At least 10 characters, not containing the name part of your email') overlaps the bottom edge of the password input and looks cramped.
findings.expected: Hint text below the field with spacing.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the hint below the input with margin.

findings.what_happened: The checklist heading reads 'Quality questions for a other study' with the wrong article. The reasoning panel says 'Quality questions for a cross-sectional study' elsewhere.
findings.expected: 'an other study' or 'an unclassified study'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a/an agreement or rephrase to 'Quality questions (study type: other)'.

findings.what_happened: The landing page does not mention demo mode, the one-paper-per-topic cap or the fact that this is a prototype. Those appear only after sign-in. The animated demo near the bottom autoplays (there is a pause button).
findings.expected: A short note on the landing page that this is a demo build with recorded samples, so first-time users are not surprised.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one line under the CTA: 'Demo build: uses recorded sample papers.' Keep the pause control.

findings.what_happened: Demo mode scripts everything to telemedicine in Southeast Asia. The searches say Southeast Asia, Thailand, Vietnam and never mention hip fracture. The three candidate questions are about rural Southeast Asia. The chosen question and the exported report headline do not match the idea I typed. The demo banner explains this once at the top, but the search page, the question cards and the export page do not say 'this does not reflect your topic'. Only small '(mock)' tags appear.
findings.expected: Where the demo output visibly contradicts the user's topic (searches, questions, export), a short local note such as 'Demo sample: not about your topic'. The exported report should carry a clear demo watermark.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a persistent, non-dismissable 'Demo sample data' line at the top of the searches, question and export pages, and a banner at the top of the downloaded report. In real mode, show a warning if a search block does not contain any of the user's concepts.

findings.what_happened: Candidates 2 and 3 are ungrammatical templates ('What older factors shape...', 'What adults factors shape...'). Candidate 2 is labelled 'a question about the effect of an exposure' but is worded as a 'factors shape implementation' question. All three have identical gap, feasibility and weakness text. A physician would think the tool is broken, and the questions look fabricated.
findings.expected: Three distinct, well-formed questions whose label matches the wording, each with its own gap, feasibility and weakness.
findings.suggested_fix: Build candidates from the whole idea and chosen topics, not single topic names. Check each candidate for grammar and for a match between structure label and wording before showing it. Flag clearly in demo mode that the scripted candidates are placeholders.

findings.what_happened: After I answered 2 questions and tapped 'Skip the rest', 'What we know so far' showed 'not answered yet' for Who, Where, What is studied and Outcome, with 'questions done' left blank. The scoping conversation still held my answers, so it looked as if my answers were lost.
findings.expected: The summary should keep my answers and show them after skipping.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the collected answers in the 'What we know so far' panel after skip. Otherwise hide the panel once skipping.

findings.what_happened: I tapped 'Appraise selected papers'. The header changed to 'Now: step 7/9' but the page still showed the step 6 ranking content and the button. There was no spinner, no toast and no 'Go to step 7'. I did not know whether it worked, and I only found step 7 by going back to the overview and tapping 'Open step 7'.
findings.expected: Move straight to the appraisal step, or show a clear 'Appraisal started, Go to step 7' message (the UX intent says a non-current panel should offer 'Go to step N').
findings.suggested_fix: After the action, navigate to the appraisal node. If it runs in the background, show live progress with a 'Go to step 7' button.

findings.what_happened: The checklist says 'Decide every quote the check could not find (14 left)' and the paper shows 'UNVERIFIED' quotes. I decided one, then tapped 'Summarise the evidence', and the app let me through with 13 undecided quotes and no warning. A phone user working under time pressure is likely to do the same. Also, the appraisal header says '14 unverified quotes to decide' while the first paper's checklist quotes show green 'verified', which looks contradictory until you find the 'Key findings' quote lower down.
findings.expected: Either require decisions, or warn: '13 quotes still undecided; they will be left out/flagged in the synthesis'. The count label should say 'papers with a quote to decide'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a confirmation listing the number of undecided quotes. Add a 'Reject all remaining unverified' bulk action. Rename the count to 'papers with quotes to decide'.

findings.what_happened: My goal was a report I could email to myself from a phone. The only report format is Markdown, which most phone users cannot open. There is no PDF, Word or 'email me this' option. After tapping 'Download the report (Markdown)' there was no visible confirmation, and I could not tell whether anything arrived. The preview does show the content, with identifiers, quotes and the novelty-check search.
findings.expected: A phone-friendly report (PDF or .docx or HTML) or a share/email option, plus a 'Downloaded' confirmation.
findings.suggested_fix: Offer PDF/.docx, or 'Email me the report'. Show a 'Report downloaded' toast and a 'Copy to clipboard' option.

findings.what_happened: Colour by offers only Study type, Topic and Source database, so I cannot colour or filter the chart by Article type. The Article type bars in the 'What kinds of papers' box are not tappable. The legend says 'hover to highlight', which does not work on a phone. The legend labels are faint. The 3D scatter is hard to read at 375 px, and its scroll area did not respond to the helper's scroll, only to keyboard PageDown.
findings.expected: On a phone, a tappable, readable way to filter by both study type and article type from the retrieval step.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the Article type bars tappable filters, and add Article type to 'Colour by' or link to the table view (step 5), where chips work well. Reword the legend hint to 'Tap to show only one'. Raise legend contrast.

findings.what_happened: The suggested topics were 'Help', 'Older', 'Adults', 'Measurement and outcomes' and 'Context and setting'. 'Hip fracture' was missing, and 'Help' is not a clinical concept. I had to find 'Add or merge topics' to add 'Hip fracture surgery', which then had 0 synonyms and 0 MeSH. Synonyms for tele-rehabilitation were only a plural. Ranking later left 'Adults' and 'Context and setting' with 0 selected papers.
findings.expected: Topics that are real concepts from my idea and answers (hip fracture, older adults, telerehabilitation), with sensible synonyms.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract noun phrases and drop stop words. Offer synonym and MeSH suggestions for user-added topics. Warn when a topic ends up with no selected papers.

findings.what_happened: The sticky panel header (step label, headline, description, progress strip) takes about a third of the 812 px screen, so I read the real content in a squeezed window. The top bar 'Now: step 1/...' is also cut off. The in-panel scroll was unreliable with the scroll helper but worked with the keyboard. Edit, Delete and Dismiss targets are small. The focus helper reported no visible focus style on the download link and the headings.

findings.what_happened: On the overview and in the retrieval step each query still shows 'PubMed – · OpenAlex –' (dashes) even after the searches ran and returned 125 and 49 papers. The paper detail also shows '? citations'. They look like missing data.
findings.expected: Counts or 'not counted' in words.
findings.suggested_fix: Show real per-query counts, and hide 'citations' when unknown (or write 'citations not available').

That was partly the test helper, but the top-left 'Overview' link and the 'Now: step 7/9' header look like the only way back. The panel's step 7 content was only reachable by going to Overview and tapping 'Open step 7'.

The step 2 illustration says 'STEP 2 OF 9' in tiny text, and the 'See a review take shape' demo canvas text is unreadable at 375 px. reports.categories_and_colours: At step 4 and in the step 5 and 6 tables I could filter by study type and by article type. In the 3D chart the legend pairs colour and shape with a count: Trial (blue circle), Systematic/scoping review (pink star), Other design (green cross), Not reported (grey ring), Cohort (orange square), Cross-sectional (green triangle), Qualitative (gold diamond). I understood this from the legend without being told, and tapping a legend entry isolated that type with a clear 'Showing only one category (3 papers). Click it again to show all.' line. Article type uses plain bars with no colour, which is clear. In the table, large chips for both study type and article type filter correctly, with a 'Showing 3 of 96: trial. 93 papers are hidden by your filters' message and a visible Reset filters. This is the clearest part of the app on a phone. Problems: Article type bars are not tappable in the retrieval step and Article type is not a 'Colour by' option; the legend says 'hover', which does not exist on a phone; the legend text is faint; 'Not reported' (ring) is 82 at retrieval and 16 after AI summaries, which is explained but could be read as the counts changing; the 3D chart is hard to read at 375 px. Counts sum correctly: study type 3+3+8+82 = 96 and article type 72+13+2+9 = 96.
reports.validity_assessment: Traceability is the app's real strength. Every paper has a DOI, PMID and the database abstract. Appraisal quotes are checked word for word. A deliberately altered quote was caught and shown red with the closest real passage and its match percentage. The scoring rubric weights are visible. The novelty check shows the exact search and record counts and states that finding none does not prove novelty. The export lists identifiers, the search strategy and the decisions made. The report states it was generated by the 'Athena prototype'. The demo is honest in one dismissible banner and '(mock)' tags. Weaknesses: (1) In demo mode the research question, searches, synthesis ('Findings differ between studies') and candidates have nothing to do with hip fracture and tele-rehabilitation, with no local warning on the question or export pages, and the exported report headline pairs my real question with an unrelated Southeast Asia question. (2) The candidate questions are malformed templates with identical rationale text. (3) The app lets users move on with undecided unverified quotes without a warning. (4) Topic extraction picks up filler words ('Help') and misses the main clinical concept. I could not judge real-mode validity. As a clinician I would not forward this report as it stands, because it does not carry a clear demo watermark at the top.
reports.would_have_quit_at: I would have kept going to the end, but with a real 15-minute window I would have quit at step 7 (Appraisal): 14 papers each with several quotes to decide is too much for a phone between ward rounds, and the app did not say I could skip. The ranking to appraisal hand-off with no feedback was the point where I was closest to giving up. At the export I would stop because the report is a Markdown file I cannot easily email or open on a phone, and the question it gives me is about Southeast Asia.
reports.activity: Created an account (Dr Okafor, okafor.clinician@example.com). Created one project (prj_9b51feebaa8a4dc5) from the idea 'Does tele-rehabilitation help older adults recover after hip fracture surgery?'. Answered 2 of 5 scoping questions and skipped the rest. Dismissed 1 suggested topic ('Help'), added 1 topic ('Hip fracture surgery') and kept 5 suggested topics. Ran all 12 database searches (174 results fetched, 78 duplicates merged, 96 papers). Started AI summaries (10 of 10 batches done). Used the study type filter and legend isolation, opened one paper, ranked the papers (16 selected) and started appraisal (14 papers). Rejected 1 unverified quote and left 13 undecided. Opened the synthesis (12 statements, 4 conflicts), chose candidate question 1 of 3, finished the review and tapped 'Download the report (Markdown)' (no visible confirmation). One client console error ('removeChild') after the step 5 summaries. No failed network requests. About 100 helper commands used. Browser stopped. Screenshots are in /home/user/athena/docs/qa/iteration-1/clinician/ (01-landing to 25-download).
reports.narrative: I landed on Athena on my phone and understood within seconds that it turns a rough idea into a research question backed by real papers. Sign-up was quick, although the password hint overlapped the input. I typed my tele-rehabilitation question and was told about demo mode up front, which I appreciated. Then I got slightly lost: I had already written my idea, yet step 1 asked me to confirm it again. The scoping questions were short and fine, but after I skipped the rest, the summary said nothing was answered, so I wondered if my answers had been lost. The suggested topics included 'Help', but not hip fracture, so I added it myself, and the Add button was fiddly. The searches then said Southeast Asia and Thailand, which clearly was not my topic. The demo note explained why, but I still felt uneasy. The retrieval numbers were clear, and the legend's colours and shapes made sense. I could filter by study and article type in the table with thumb-sized chips, which I liked, though the 3D chart was too small and its legend asked me to hover. Ranking showed a visible scoring rubric, which built trust. After I tapped 'Appraise selected papers' nothing visibly happened and I had to hunt for step 7. The appraisal was the best part for trust, because it caught an altered quote and showed the real passage next to it. But 14 papers is a lot on a phone, and the app let me skip 13 undecided quotes without a warning. The three candidate questions were obviously broken templates. The export gave me Markdown only, with no way to email it and no confirmation after I tapped download.

reports.would_have_quit_at: I would not have quit, but I would have stopped trusting the result at step 9. My question was about diabetes in Thailand and the chosen research question was about "telemedicine implementation in rural Southeast Asia". The app gave no clear warning that the review no longer matched my idea, and nothing told me what to do about it. If I had hit the stale step-6 page after "Appraise selected papers", with no button to go forward, I would have been close to quitting there.
reports.activity: I created the account somchai.pharm24@example.com and one project (prj_2d4f50c522a14bfb). I typed the idea exactly as given and answered 3 of the up-to-5 scoping questions. I deleted one suggested topic by accident ("Mobile" instead of "Help", because the helper's click took the first Delete). I added 2 topics by hand ("Mobile health app" and "Type 2 diabetes in Thailand"). I ran 14 searches (118 unique papers, 177 duplicates merged) and let the AI summarise all 118. I filtered the table by study type and article type, opened 2 papers, ranked, and appraised 14 papers. I tried to reject many unverified quotes, though the counter never changed. I opened the synthesis, chose candidate question 1, reached the export page, previewed the report and clicked Download. Console errors: 2 "removeChild" page errors, one when Summarise finished (step 4 to 5) and one after "Appraise selected papers" (step 6 to 7). I saw no failed requests. About 100 helper commands in total.
reports.categories_and_colours: Study type has a clear legend: blue circle = Trial, orange square = Cohort / case-control, teal triangle = Cross-sectional, amber diamond = Qualitative / mixed methods, pink star = Systematic / scoping review, green cross = Other design, grey ring = Not reported. Each has a text label and a count, and the key says "hover to highlight, click to show only that category". This was understandable without being told. Article type (Journal article, Review article, Preprint, Editorial / letter / comment) has no colour. It appears as counts and filter chips on retrieval, the table and the ranking page. I could filter by both study type and article type in the table. The "Colour by" dropdown offers Study type, Topic and Source database (plus Ranking score at step 6). It has no Article type option, which matches the intent doc. Problems I found: (1) the same blue circle means "Trial" under Study type but "App" under Topic, so I had to re-read the key each time I switched. (2) Teal triangle and green cross are two similar greens. (3) Study-type counts shift a lot between step 4 (Not reported 98) and step 5 (Not reported 17), and the app only says the AI reads every abstract in the next step. The 3D scatter has no labelled y axis at step 4 ("Height has no meaning yet"). (4) Filter chips are combined with AND. "Showing 0 of 118: trial; review article" gives no hint that Trial AND Review article cannot both be true. (5) In the topic colouring, "Context and setting" and "Type 2 diabetes in Thailand" are greyed with no count, so they have 0 papers. I was never told why my own topic found nothing, yet at step 6 it showed "4 selected".
reports.validity_assessment: Traceability is good. Every paper shows DOI, PMID, PMCID and OpenAlex ID, the abstract as returned by the database, and a Full text or Abstract only badge. Quotes carry a verified or unverified badge, "Show source" and "Open paper". Unverified quotes are not hidden: the app shows "UNVERIFIED: Quote not found" and lets you Reject, Undo or Accept anyway. The novelty check says "what was found, not proof of novelty", which is the right caveat. The demo-mode banner is dismissible and appears on every page, and AI text is tagged "(mock)". The landing page says nothing about demo mode, and the retrieval counts (e.g. "PubMed 2,207 papers match") have no (mock) tag. Validity problems: (1) The chosen question ("(mock) What app factors shape telemedicine implementation in rural Southeast Asia?") has dropped everything specific in my idea (diabetes, blood sugar, Thailand, patients). The search queries contain only "telemedicine", "Southeast Asia", "app". Nowhere is the user warned that the review no longer matches their idea. Demo mode explains this on the banner, but a real user would not know whether to trust it. (2) Papers on teledentistry, glaucoma, yoga, HIV, stuttering and smoking cessation are "selected for appraisal", one with score 28 and no abstract. There is no low-score or no-abstract warning. (3) A quote marked "verified" can still be irrelevant to the checklist question. The "Confounders identified" answer is backed by a verified quote about "By 2050, Singapore is projected to have 1 million people with diabetes", so "verified" only means the words exist in the text, not that they support the answer. (4) One unverified quote reads "Quote not found ... Closest passage (100% of words match)", which contradicts itself. (5) The synthesis is placeholder ("(mock) Placeholder contradiction..." for every topic, 1 conflict each, with a protocol sentence "results will be published in peer-reviewed journals" as the evidence). It is labelled mock, but it looks like a real conflict finding. (6) The unverified-quote counter ("25 left") and the per-paper "N unverified" never decreased after Reject, so I could not tell whether my decisions counted. (7) The report intro says "AI-extracted claims carry verbatim quotes that were checked against the retrieved text", which is true only for verified quotes. (8) The review is only as valid as its topics. My idea words were split into "Mobile", "App", "Help", "Diabtes", and the typo survived as a topic name.
reports.narrative: I opened Athena at tablet width. The landing page told me quickly that this is a tool that turns a rough idea into a research question using real papers. I clicked Start a review and signed up. The password hint text sat on top of the password box, which looked broken, but I got through. I typed my idea with its mistakes. The app then showed my own idea back to me and asked me to "Open step 1", where I had to confirm the same sentence again. That felt odd, but "Start scoping" got me moving. The AI asked three questions. Some were hard for me: "Which years and kinds of studies should count, for example 2015 onwards, any design including interviews and reviews?" is two questions in one, with an idiom. It copied my "who" answer into "where", and it turned my words into the topics "Mobile", "App", "Help" and "Diabtes". I could not open a topic to fix the spelling. The list showed plain text with no clear way to open it. Later the editor appeared by itself. I accidentally deleted a topic, and there was no undo. The search builder was heavy with words like "index term", "MeSH", "group 1 any of" and "title/abstract". Retrieval was good: clear numbers, a mix chart, and a colour legend I understood. The 3D chart was fine. The summary table, filters, paper details and ranking rubric were clear. After "Appraise selected papers" the page froze on step 6 while the top bar said step 7, and a console error appeared. I had to go back to the overview to continue. The appraisal text was honest about abstract-only papers, and unverified quotes were flagged in red. The final question was not about diabetes at all. I downloaded the report, but nothing told me the download worked.

'295 results fetched, 177 the same paper found twice, so 118 different papers remain' is very clear. Mix bars and legend were clear.

Many controls at once. 'Context and setting 0 selected' in orange gave no explanation. The list is not sorted by score even though the page talks about ranking.
Good instructions, but the amount of text, 'quotes the check could not find', 'Accept anyway' and the 25-left counter that never changed were confusing.
Known, contested and unknown by topic. The content was clearly placeholder.
