Three formats with plain descriptions and a preview. 'Markdown opens in Word' is doubtful, and clicking Download gave no visible feedback.

findings.what_happened: After clicking 'Appraise selected papers' the top bar changed to 'Now: step 7/9 · Appraisal', but the page kept showing the step 6 content ('Check which papers go forward'). The 'Appraise selected papers' button vanished and no 'Go to step 7' button appeared. A reload kept the stale step 6 content and reset its checklist to 0 of 3. The console showed a page error: Failed to execute 'removeChild' on 'Node'. The same error appeared once after 'Summarise the papers' (step 4 to 5), where I could still continue. I only escaped by going to the overview and using 'Open step 7'.
findings.expected: The page moves to step 7, or a clear 'Go to step 7' button appears, as the UX intent doc says no page should be a dead end. No page errors.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the unmount error (likely the 3D/canvas teardown or a portal) so the table page navigates to the new step. Add a 'Go to step N' button on any panel whose step is not current.

findings.what_happened: The chosen question, and the whole review, had nothing to do with my idea. My idea was diabetes patients, Thailand and blood sugar. The question was '(mock) What app factors shape telemedicine implementation in rural Southeast Asia?'. The generated searches contain 'telemedicine' and 'Southeast Asia' but not diabetes. Papers on teledentistry, glaucoma, yoga and HIV were 'selected for appraisal'. Demo mode explains this on the banner, but in the flow there is no 'low relevance to your idea' check.
findings.expected: At least a visible check that the chosen question and the selected papers match the user's original idea, and a warning when they do not. Even in demo mode the final question should reflect the idea.
findings.suggested_fix: Show an 'idea vs question' match check at step 9 and warn when key terms are missing. In demo mode, state this on the question card, not only in the banner. Make the scripted demo substitute the user's key terms.

findings.what_happened: The counters 'Decide every quote the check could not find (25 left)' and '25 unverified quotes to decide' never went down after I clicked Reject on many unverified quotes. The per-paper chips still read '3 unverified' for paper 1 after I rejected one. I could not tell whether my decisions were recorded or whether the 'Decide' checklist item could ever be completed.
findings.expected: The counter drops as each quote is accepted or rejected, and the checklist item completes when none is left.
findings.suggested_fix: Count only undecided quotes. Show 'N decided, M left'. Show 'rejected by you' in the per-paper chips.

findings.what_happened: 'verified' only means the quote text exists in the paper, not that it answers the checklist question. For 'Confounders identified and adjusted for' (AI: Unclear), the verified quote is about Singapore saving $15 million by 2050. One unverified quote says 'Quote not found ... Closest passage (100% of words match)', which contradicts itself. The cohort checklist was also applied to an economic modelling study.
findings.expected: A 'verified' badge should say what it proves. Contradictory messages should not appear. The checklist should fit the study design.
findings.suggested_fix: Label the badge 'quote found in text' and add a separate 'does this support the answer?' prompt. Fix the 100%-match message. Choose the checklist by design, with a fallback for modelling studies.

findings.what_happened: Papers far from the topic (teledentistry, glaucoma, yoga, hematopathology, HIV) are pre-selected, including one with score 28 and 'no abstract available'. The list for a topic is alphabetical, not sorted by score, although the page is about ranking. 'Context and setting 0 selected' appears in orange with no explanation.
findings.expected: Rank order by score, a warning for low-scoring or abstract-less papers that are selected, and a hint on what to do for a topic with 0 selected.
findings.suggested_fix: Sort by score by default and show the rank. Flag selected papers with a score below a threshold or with no abstract. Explain '0 selected'.

findings.what_happened: The AI turned my sentence into the topics 'Mobile', 'App', 'Help', 'Diabtes', 'Measurement and outcomes', 'Context and setting'. My typo became a topic name and 'Help' became a topic. The answers I gave were echoed into the wrong boxes ('Who' and 'Where' show the same text, and 'Which years' and 'Which kinds of studies' show the same text). After 'Keep', the topic rows lost their Edit/Delete buttons, and the text said 'Open a topic to edit its name and synonyms', but my clicks on the topic names timed out. The editor then opened by itself on 'Use these topics', with the label 'Viewing step 2 of 9 · Scoping' under a 'Now: step 3' header.
findings.expected: Sensible topics, spelling cleaned, answers in the right boxes. A visible way to edit a topic. A consistent step label.
findings.suggested_fix: Show an obvious 'Edit' on each topic in the approval screen, make topic rows look clickable, drop stop-words like 'help', and correct or flag obvious typos. Split the multi-part question.

findings.what_happened: Clicking 'Delete' removes a topic immediately with no confirmation, no undo and no toast. I removed the wrong one when two rows had the same button name.
findings.expected: Undo or a confirmation, and an accessible name per row (e.g. 'Delete Help').
findings.suggested_fix: Give each button a row-specific accessible name and show 'Deleted X. Undo' for a few seconds.

findings.what_happened: I typed my idea on /s/new. The next screen asked 'Tell us what you want to research' with my idea already in it as 'Draft idea', and 'Start scoping' to confirm. 'Scoping' is jargon, and '8 s' next to 'What happens in this step' looked like a time estimate for the step.
findings.expected: After 'Start my review' go straight to the first question, or explain why the idea needs to be confirmed. Use plain words ('Ask me questions') and label the video length ('8 s video').
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the button, skip the repeat step, and label the '8 s' as a video.

findings.what_happened: Question 3 is two questions at once with idioms: 'Which years and kinds of studies should count — for example 2015 onwards, any design including interviews and reviews?'. The header says 'up to 5 short questions' and then '5 more to cover' after question 1.
findings.expected: One short plain question at a time with simple words.
findings.suggested_fix: Split into 'Which years?' and 'What kinds of study (surveys, trials, reviews)?' and use 'from 2015 to now' instead of '2015 onwards'.

findings.what_happened: Heavy jargon for a non-native reader: 'index term', 'title/abstract', 'group 1: any of ... AND group 2', 'MeSH', 'controlled vocabulary'. The query for the topic 'App' includes 'telemedicine' and 'Southeast Asia' that I never wrote. PubMed shows 2 groups and OpenAlex shows 3 for the same topic. The count '2,207 papers match' has no (mock) tag. After running all searches the query rows still read 'PubMed – · OpenAlex –', and only the first topic's PubMed count appears.
findings.expected: Plain explanation of the groups, queries that match my topic, and query rows that show the counts after the run.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-line plain explanation above the groups ('a paper must match one word from each box'). Update the query rows after the run. Tag demo numbers as mock.

findings.what_happened: The helper text 'At least 10 characters, not containing the name part of your email.' overlaps the bottom of the Password input, so it looks broken. The rule is also hard to understand ('name part of your email').
findings.expected: Hint below the field and not on top of it, in simpler words.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the layout and write 'At least 10 characters. Do not use your email name.'

findings.what_happened: Choosing 'Trial' and 'Review article' gives 'Showing 0 of 118: trial; review article.' with no hint that the groups are combined with AND, so I thought something was wrong.
findings.expected: A plain explanation such as 'papers that are Trial AND Review article'.
findings.suggested_fix: Show 'Trial AND Review article: no paper matches both' and offer to switch the second group off.

findings.what_happened: The colours change meaning when 'Colour by' changes (blue circle = Trial under Study type, blue circle = App under Topic). Teal triangle and green cross are two similar greens. The article type, which is a main thing I wanted to filter by, cannot be used to colour the map. The study type counts change from step 4 (Not reported 98) to step 5 (Not reported 17) without a clear explanation.
findings.expected: The legend always shows which dimension is being coloured. The AI relabelling is explained where the numbers change.
findings.suggested_fix: Put the dimension name in the legend heading ('Colour: study type'). Say 'AI labels added from abstracts' next to the changed counts.

findings.what_happened: Every topic shows '1 conflict', 'Placeholder contradiction between two papers' key findings', and the Known statement '(mock) 7 key findings were extracted for this topic.' The quote chips lead to a protocol sentence ('The results of this study will be published in peer-reviewed journals'). It is labelled mock, but it looks like a real finding and does not help a student.
findings.expected: In demo mode, a clear 'sample output' tag on the whole card, or a sensible demo.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark the whole synthesis block as a demo sample. Skip protocol-only papers when building 'findings'.

findings.what_happened: The page says 'Pick one; you can edit it' and 'you can edit it after', but I found no edit control on the chosen question or on the export page. 'PICo (Population, phenomenon of Interest, Context)' is jargon.
findings.expected: A visible 'Edit question' button next to 'Chosen'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an Edit button on the chosen card, or remove the promise. Explain PICo in plain words.

findings.what_happened: The report is called 'Markdown, a text document: opens in Word, Google Docs or any text editor'. A student would not know what Markdown is, and .md files do not normally open in Word. Clicking 'Download the report (Markdown)' showed no confirmation, so I could not tell it worked. In the preview the Gap line shows broken italics ('c5b39fb8454e549de]' partly italic) and raw ids in square brackets.
findings.expected: A Word-friendly format or an honest note, a visible 'downloaded' message, and a clean preview.
findings.suggested_fix: Offer .docx or PDF, show a toast on download, escape the ids in the preview and show readable citations.

findings.what_happened: The landing page does not say it is a demo, so a new user could expect real results on their topic until they see the banner after signing in. Words like 'appraised' and 'synthesis' are hard for a second-language reader.
findings.expected: One line near the first button such as 'Demo version: sample papers on a different topic'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the demo note on the landing page when the server is in demo mode, and simplify 'appraise' to 'check quality'.

findings.what_happened: The paper detail shows 'Trials' as the article type next to 'Randomised trial' as the study type. 'Key finding' for a trial protocol shows only a registry number ('NCT07198828.') or a truncated sentence ending in 'and'. The model name 'mock:grok-4.20-0309-reasoning' is shown under Details.
findings.expected: Consistent labels and complete key findings, with technical details only for those who ask.
findings.suggested_fix: Trim key findings at a sentence end, show 'Protocol, no results yet', and keep model names behind a Details control.

findings.what_happened: Compared to the intent doc: (a) 'A panel whose step is not the current one offers Go to step N' did not hold on the stale step 6 page. (b) 'Keep or delete each suggested topic, open one to edit' was not discoverable. (c) 'Detail sits behind Details or ⋯' was mostly true, but jargon was visible on the search builder (MeSH, index term). (d) The categories and colours rules (shape plus label plus legend, click to isolate, article type without hue) matched what I understood, and I could say 'the colours and shapes show the kind of study'. (e) Retrieval, summary table, export and demo banner matched their intent.
findings.expected: Pages match the intended 3-second reading.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the items above and keep the categories rules as they are.

findings.what_happened: After almost every action (open step, send answer, keep topics, approve, choose a question) focus drops to the page body or lands on a heading with no visible focus style. The answer box is never focused automatically. My first typed answer went into a collapsed 'What happens in this step' button and was lost. Tab from the body then jumps to an unpredictable control (sometimes the textarea, sometimes the primary button), and the next Tab leaves the panel to the header.
findings.expected: After each action focus moves to the next logical control (the answer box, or the new panel's primary action), with a visible ring. At least the panel heading should show a focus outline.
findings.suggested_fix: Programmatically focus the first interactive control (answer textarea or primary action) after each panel change. Give focused headings a visible outline, or focus the container with a skip hint. Do not let a button that becomes disabled ('Chosen') drop focus to the body.

findings.page: Summary and ranking (/table) after pressing 'Appraise selected papers'
findings.what_happened: After pressing Appraise selected papers and waiting about 14 seconds, the page showed no change: the top bar said step 7/9 but the content was still step 6, the sticky action button vanished and no 'Go to step 7' or progress message appeared. I had to guess that the 'Overview' link would show a way forward, then press 'Go to step 7: Appraisal' there.
findings.expected: Either move to the appraisal step, or show a running state ('Appraising 13 papers...') and a visible next action.
findings.suggested_fix: Show a progress or running banner, then navigate to the appraisal view or show 'Go to step 7' on this page. This also matches the intent doc's 'no page is a dead end'.

findings.page: Scoping approved panel -> 'Go to step 3: Search builder'
findings.what_happened: Pressing 'Go to step 3: Search builder' opened 'Edit this search topic: Peer' (a topic editor) with the header still reading 'Viewing step 2 of 9 - Done'. I thought I had gone to the wrong place and needed to press 'Write the searches' without knowing why.
findings.expected: 'Go to step 3' opens the step-3 search builder overview, labelled step 3.
findings.suggested_fix: Route to the step-3 landing view, or update the header and heading to say this is the first topic's search and that 'Write the searches' creates queries for all topics.

findings.what_happened: After I answered two scoping questions, the summary said 'not answered yet' for every field and '0 of 6 answered', so my answers looked lost. The suggested topics were single words ('Peer', 'Support', 'Groups', 'Postpartum') plus generic 'Measurement and outcomes' and 'Context and setting'. 'Depression' and 'low-income' were missing. The 'Peer' search string contained 'telemedicine' as an index term. None of this is flagged next to the topic.
findings.expected: My answers appear under who, where and outcome, and topics are meaningful concepts (e.g. 'peer support groups', 'postpartum depression', 'low- and middle-income countries'). Any mock substitution is flagged where it appears.
findings.suggested_fix: Show the answers I gave in 'What we know so far'. In demo mode, label the topic and query lists as scripted ('(mock) not derived from your answers') and explain why telemedicine terms appear. In live mode, validate that topics are phrases.

findings.page: Appraisal to Synthesis (step 7 to 8) and Research question
findings.what_happened: The landing page promises every quote is 'checked against its source' and the appraisal asks me to decide 13 unverified quotes, yet I looked at 0 of 13 papers, decided 0 quotes and pressed 'Summarise the evidence' straight through. The synthesis and questions were still built from them. In the one paper I opened, a quote about public uptake of apps was used under 'Risk of bias assessed', so a 'verified' quote did not support its answer. The chosen question is about telemedicine though my idea was postpartum depression, and the report title and question disagree.
findings.expected: Undecided quotes block or clearly warn before synthesis. 'Verified' should say only that the words exist in the text, not that they support the answer. The final report should flag a mismatch between idea and question.
findings.suggested_fix: On 'Summarise the evidence' show 'N quotes still undecided. They will be left out' and require confirmation. Reword the verified badge to 'wording found in text'. In demo mode add a banner inside the report and the research-question step that the question does not match the user's idea.

findings.what_happened: At 200% zoom the password hint ('At least 10 characters, not containing the name part of your email.') overlaps the bottom of the password input and sits over the typed dots, hard to read for low vision. The focus ring surrounds both.
findings.expected: The hint sits below the field with space between.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the hint normal flow with margin-top, or make the label/input/hint a column grid with gap; do not position the hint over the input.

findings.page: Step side panel at 200% zoom (all steps)
findings.what_happened: At 200% zoom on a 1366x900 screen the panel's scrollable content area is only about 350-450px high. The header block (title, text, 9-segment strip) and the footer buttons take most of the screen, and the sticky demo note takes more. Lists and cards are viewed through a letterbox, and I often could not see what was focused without scrolling. The paper/ranking pages have a sticky top bar, note and bottom button that leave about half the screen.
findings.expected: Headers shrink or scroll with content at high zoom so the working area is most of the viewport.
findings.suggested_fix: Below roughly 1000px effective width make the panel header non-sticky (scroll away) and collapse the step description. Let the demo note scroll away once seen.

findings.what_happened: Escape closes the drawer correctly and the drawer traps Tab, but focus does not return to the paper row I opened. It falls to the body and the next Tab goes back to 'Skip to content', so I would have to tab through dozens of rows again.
findings.expected: Focus returns to the row that opened the drawer.
findings.suggested_fix: Store document.activeElement before opening the drawer and restore it on close.

findings.what_happened: Each paper has about 30 tab stops (a 'Show source' and 'Pin to canvas' per quality question) before I reach 'Summarise the evidence'. I tabbed about 40 times from the top of the panel with no shortcut. Both footer buttons look similar, so I was unsure which was primary until I found 'Next paper'. 'Click a chip' and 'Click the arrow' hints are mouse-first.
findings.expected: A landmark or skip link to 'Next paper / Summarise' and keyboard-oriented hint wording.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'Skip to actions' inside the panel, collapse per-question buttons into a single disclosure, and word hints as 'select' or 'press Enter'.

findings.what_happened: Console reported a page error 'Failed to execute removeChild on Node: The node to be removed is not a child of this node' when I pressed 'Summarise the papers' while the 3D/2D chart was on the page. The step still worked.
findings.expected: No console errors.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the chart teardown (Three.js or SVG container) for double removal on unmount.

findings.what_happened: The page says the top 3-5 papers per topic are selected, but 'Groups' and 'Context and setting' show 0 selected and the checklist shows '0 of 3 done'. No warning appeared before 'Appraise selected papers'. My Journal-article filter from step 5 silently stayed on ('Showing 29 of 44'), and the filter text was easy to miss. The Overview later said '16 selected' but appraisal listed 13 papers.
findings.expected: A warning when a topic has none, filters reset when entering a new step or announced prominently, and consistent counts.
findings.suggested_fix: Warn about topics with fewer than 3 selected, announce active filters in a live region at the top, and explain 16 vs 13.

findings.what_happened: 'Colour by' offers Study type, Topic and Source database only, so I cannot colour or filter by article type there. Article type appears only as counts, with filters in the later table step. In Topic mode the legend says 'Peer 36, Support 4, Postpartum 4', which implies 36 papers are about peer support when they are demo telemedicine papers. The hint 'hover to highlight' does not mention keyboard focus.
findings.expected: Article type is reachable as a view in the paper list or clearly pointed to. Legend hint mentions keyboard.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the hint to 'hover, focus or click'; add a pointer from the article-type counts to the table filters; in demo mode caveat topic counts.

findings.what_happened: The paper header shows '? citations', which reads as broken, and 'Found in pubmed' is lower case.
findings.expected: 'Citation count not available' and 'Found in PubMed'.
findings.suggested_fix: Hide the field when unknown or say 'citation count unavailable'; use proper brand capitalisation.

findings.page: Step 1 / New review and project overview
findings.what_happened: After I typed my idea and pressed 'Start my review', the overview said 'Your next step: Tell us what you want to research - Open step 1', asking me to confirm text I just entered. The example chips sit between the textarea and 'Start my review', costing three extra tabs.
findings.expected: Typing the idea and starting should move on to scoping, with the examples after or out of the tab order before the primary button.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip the redundant step-1 confirmation, or reword the step-1 panel to 'Confirm your idea'. Move example chips below the primary button in DOM order.

findings.what_happened: The report is described as 'Markdown, a text document: opens in Word, Google Docs or any text editor.' A Markdown file does not render in Word. After pressing Download there was no visible confirmation or toast, so I could not tell whether it saved. The tab order is fine and the in-page preview with 'first 200 of 799 lines' is helpful.
findings.expected: Honest format wording, and a short 'Download started' message.
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'plain text with simple formatting; paste it into Word or Google Docs' (or offer .docx), and show a live-region message after download.

findings.what_happened: The report's scoping section repeats my 'who' answer as both 'population' and 'setting'. The 'novelty check' lists unrelated results (dementia care, veterinary volunteering, digital pathology) marked 'already in your review'. It is caveated as not proof of novelty, which is good, but it looks odd.
findings.expected: Scoping fields correspond to what I wrote and the novelty list makes sense or is labelled as demo data.
findings.suggested_fix: Map answers to fields correctly, or label unclassified answers; in demo mode, label the novelty list 'sample results'.

three_second_test.note: Heading and two buttons make it clear it turns a rough idea into a research question backed by real papers. First action is Start a review; skip link and focus ring are visible.
Plain form, but the password hint overlaps the field at 200% zoom.
Describe the idea, then Start my review. The textarea is auto-focused, which is good. Example chips sit in the tab path before the button.
A list with 'Open step 1' for the idea I just typed. I was unsure why I was asked again.
Confirm the idea and press Start scoping, but it duplicates the previous page and the panel fills the screen at 200%.
Answer the question and press Send. Focus is not in the answer box, so my first typing was lost.

three_second_test.page: Keep suggested topics / Use these topics
three_second_test.note: Keep or edit topics then approve. The single-word topics are not understandable as search topics for my subject.
Check searches then Run all 12. The 'telemedicine' term in my 'Peer' query was confusing.
Counts of found and duplicate papers; legend with shapes and counts is clear. Chart reached by keyboard through the legend.
Table of papers with a 3-item checklist and filter chips; chip wording is mouse-oriented.
Focus landed on the bottom button of a long list and the 3-5 per topic rule conflicts with 0 selected in two topics; unclear what to do.
Heavy: many quote cards, 13 undecided quotes and no obvious route. I understood it is a per-paper checklist but not what was required.
Known / contested / unknown with quote chips and a clear 'Suggest research questions' action.
Three candidates with gap, feasibility, weakness and a novelty caveat; Finish and export is locked until choose, which is clear.
Pick a format and download; a preview is shown. Markdown described as opening in Word.

reports.categories_and_colours: Study type has a colour, a shape and a text label in the legend (Trial blue circle, Cohort orange square, Cross-sectional green triangle, Qualitative amber diamond, Systematic/scoping review pink star, Other design green cross, Not reported grey ring). I understood the legend without being told, and unused categories are dimmed. The legend is reachable and operable by keyboard as buttons with counts, and the active article-type filter shows a tick icon as well as a fill, so state is not colour alone. In the table I could filter by study type and by article type (Journal article 29, Review article 6, Preprint 2, Editorial/letter/comment 7), and the page said 'Showing 29 of 44: journal article. 15 papers are hidden by your filters (still in the review)' with a Reset filters button. Problems: (1) at retrieval the Colour by menu has no Article type option and the legend hint says 'hover to highlight', which is mouse-first; (2) the Peer/Support/Postpartum topic colours in the demo imply 36 papers on 'peer', which is misleading; (3) a filter set in step 5 silently persists into step 6; (4) the 3D canvas itself cannot be navigated by keyboard (only the legend and 2D toggle can), though the 2D alternative is offered; (5) the retrieval counts (Not reported 34) differ from the table counts after AI summary (Not reported 12), which is explained in the page text and was not confusing.
reports.validity_assessment: Traceability is strong where it exists: each paper has real DOI/PMID/PMCID links, every appraisal answer has a quote, and 'Show source' opens the paper text with the exact quote highlighted. The novelty check carries the caveat 'Finding none does not prove a question is new.' The demo-mode note is honest and mock text is labelled '(mock)'. The workflow is not yet valid as a review in demo mode: topics did not use my answers, the retrieved papers are telemedicine and teledentistry, the chosen question is about telemedicine, and the report title and question disagree. More importantly, the process does not enforce its own checks: I advanced from appraisal to synthesis with 0 of 13 flagged quotes decided and 0 papers looked at, two topics had no selected papers, and a 'verified' quote can sit under a question it does not answer (word-for-word found is not the same as supports). Statements like 'every quote checked against its source' on the landing page need softening or these gates need enforcing. In live mode I cannot say, but the UI would need the topic extraction and gating fixed to be defensible. Nothing looked fabricated beyond the declared mock data, though the 'Placeholder contradiction... generated to demo' in synthesis shows invented conflicts in demo.
reports.would_have_quit_at: Step 6 to 7 (Ranking, then Appraisal). After pressing 'Appraise selected papers' nothing happened on the page for 14 seconds and the sticky button disappeared, so a real user would likely give up or reload. The 200% zoom letterbox, focus loss after each step and the 30-tab-stops-per-paper appraisal would also wear down a keyboard-only user before step 7.
reports.activity: Created one account (ruth.lecturer.qa1@example.com) and one project (prj_5ab3567e15e24b86) titled 'Peer support groups for postpartum depression in low-income countries'. Answered 2 of 5 scoping questions, skipped the rest, kept 6 suggested topics, ran all 12 searches (44 unique papers), summarised the papers (4 batches), ranked, appraised (13 papers), synthesised (12 statements, 4 conflicts), chose candidate 1 and finished the export. Toggled the 2D chart and Colour by, filtered the table by article type (Journal article), opened one paper drawer, and used 'Show source' on one quote. Opened the report preview (200 of 799 lines) and activated the 'Download the report (Markdown)' link. Used about 130 helper commands, all keyboard-only (Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Escape, ArrowDown, type). One console page error seen: 'removeChild: The node to be removed is not a child of this node' on summarise. No failed network requests. Screenshots 01-40 saved under docs/qa/iteration-1/keyboard/. Browser stopped.
reports.narrative: I started with the landing page and understood it straight away: turn a rough idea into a research question backed by real papers. Tab revealed a skip link, then Log in, then Start a review, each with a clear white focus ring. At sign-up the password hint was printed on top of the password box at 200% zoom, which was hard for me to read, but the form worked and I was taken to step 1 with the textarea already focused, which I liked. After Start my review I was shown a project overview asking me to open step 1 and confirm the idea I had just typed, which felt like a repeat. From there my keyboard journey got harder. After nearly every action, focus fell to the page body and Tab went somewhere unpredictable. I typed my scoping answer while focus was on a collapsed button and lost it, then found that the page's 'what we know so far' said nothing was answered. The search topics were single words and the 'Peer' search mentioned telemedicine. The side panel at 200% zoom left only a narrow strip to read, and the ranking-to-appraisal step seemed to hang with no message. I found 'Overview' and a Go to step 7 button to continue. The appraisal had about thirty tab stops per paper, but 'Show source' with a highlighted quote was excellent for trust. I got through synthesis, chose a question and reached the export, where the preview and download worked, though the question was about telemedicine and there was no download confirmation. The demo note was honest throughout.

findings.what_happened: For my topic (short-form video, teenagers) the generated PubMed search required 'telemedicine' (index term) AND 'Asia, Southeastern / Thailand / Vietnam / Indonesia / Malaysia'. OpenAlex had three AND groups: telemedicine/telehealth, video, Southeast Asia. The only explanation is a tiny grey line '(mock) Topic synonyms AND Southeast Asia block.' Nothing warns that these terms do not come from my idea.
findings.expected: Search terms that come from my idea and my scoping answers (teenagers, attention). In demo mode, a clear flag next to the search that these terms are sample terms and not mine.
findings.suggested_fix: In demo mode put a visible 'sample search, not built from your idea' badge on each query. In real mode, test that every concept block traces back to a topic or a scoping answer, and show which one.

findings.what_happened: The chosen question is '(mock) What video factors shape telemedicine implementation in rural Southeast Asia?' (population 'Patients and providers'). The exported report preview says 'Every paper below comes from a database API record ... reports.categories_and_colours: Study type has a colour and a shape and a text label in every view I checked, and the legend is always shown. Trial = blue circle, Systematic/scoping review = pink star, Other design = green plus, Cohort/case-control = orange square, Cross-sectional = green triangle, Qualitative/mixed methods = amber diamond, Not reported = grey ring. I understood it without being told: the shape plus the text label in the legend and chips made the colours safe to read, and zero-count categories are greyed. Click-to-isolate is stated ('hover to highlight, click to show only that category'); I verified filtering through the chips in the table, with a clear 'Showing 0 of 73' message and Reset. Topic colouring (Video blue circle, Apps orange square, Attention green triangle, Measurement amber diamond, Context and setting pink star) also works with shapes. Weak spots: (1) Article type has no colour or shape at all in the retrieval bars (plain grey) and is missing from the 'Colour by' list on the maps, although it is filterable by chips in the table; clicking the article-type bars in step 4 does nothing. (2) 'Review article 8' versus 'Systematic / scoping review 5' are two different measures of review papers, which looks contradictory without a note. (3) 'Other design' is vague and its colour (green) is close to the green triangle for Cross-sectional in some lights. (4) Counts across views differ (Video 5 in the legend vs 40 in the topic view). (5) Study type counts change from step 4 (Not reported 56) to step 5 (Not reported 14) because the AI read abstracts; step 4 says so in one line, which is honest. (6) 3D points are very small, and the topic legend scrolled out of view in the panel.
reports.validity_assessment: Strong on traceability mechanics, weak on topical relevance in this demo. Good: the demo-mode banner is announced and dismissible, AI text is tagged '(mock)', the AI-drafted label sits next to each table row, the abstract expands in place, the scoring rubric is visible (weights sum to 100), every quote chip opens the exact words with a 'verified' status and 'Open paper', Show source highlights the passage in the paper text, and a planted fabricated quote was flagged as unverified with the closest real passage (54% word match) so I could Reject it. The novelty check shows real search strings and counts and carries the caveat 'Finding none does not prove a question is new'; nothing is called novel. Duplicate arithmetic checked out (160 + 55 = 215, 56 + 17 = 73, 215 − 142 = 73; type and topic counts sum to 73). Not good: (a) the whole review is about telemedicine in Southeast Asia while my topic was teenagers and short-form video. The banner explains it, but the search strings, topics, final question and exported report all present telemedicine as if it were my review, and the export does not say it is demo data. (b) My scoping answers were dropped and never used. (c) 'verified' only means the quote is in the text; some verified quotes (FUNDING, TITLE) do not support the answer they are attached to, and the checklist type (cohort) does not fit an economic modelling study. (d) I could skip 10 unresolved flagged quotes and still reach step 9 and export with step 7 'Approved'. (e) The three candidate questions are templated and nearly identical. (f) Counts in places are inconsistent (11 left vs 10, 40 vs 5, 60). So the workflow could produce a traceable review in real mode, but in this build the checks can be bypassed and the result would look more validated than it is. Privacy: the other person's project (and variants /table and /export) shows the same 'Project not found' as a made-up id, when logged out it redirects to login, and /admin sent me to My projects, so I found no leak.
reports.would_have_quit_at: I did not quit. A real student would most likely have hesitated or quit at the search builder (step 3) on seeing 'telemedicine' and 'Southeast Asia' in the search for a teenagers and short-form video topic, and again at step 7 where the checklist, counters and 'verified' badges do not agree. Without the demo banner they would have left there.

Disruptive actions: double-clicks on Start my review, Create account, Start scoping, Write the searches, Rank the papers and Reject; reload on the topics step and on the running search step; browser Back after the topics and after summarising (returned to My projects, reopened from the list, state kept); edited an approved step later; abandoned and came back from the project list. Browser stopped.
reports.narrative: I landed on Athena and understood it in a few seconds: type a rough idea, get a research question backed by real papers. Before signing up I tried the other person's project URL and got sent to a login page. After I signed up (short password first, rejected clearly, though the hint overlaps the box), the app sent me straight into that foreign URL and showed 'Project not found', the same message as for a made-up id, so I could not tell it exists. Good. I started a review and double-clicked everything: no duplicate projects, no double sends. The canvas felt busy, with three ways to go on. Scoping lost my answers, and the topics were just single words from my sentence. Editing an approved topic quietly reopened step 2 without telling me why. The search builder shocked me: telemedicine and Southeast Asia terms in a search about teenagers and TikTok. The demo banner explained it, but a real user would be lost. I liked the retrieval page and the table: counts add up, study type has colour plus shape plus label, and chips filter well. Article type could not be coloured on the maps. Ranking showed a clear rubric. Appraisal was the best idea and the most confusing page: the fabricated quote was flagged with the closest passage and I rejected it, but the counter stayed at 11, 'verified' quotes did not always support the answer, and I could skip 10 open quotes and still finish. Step 9 candidates were templated. The export previewed fine, though it never says it is demo data. I reloaded, went back, abandoned and returned: state always came back, with two silent JavaScript errors in the console.

findings.what_happened: A new user on a server with AI off sees a calm amber banner (good) saying 'AI is paused by the administrator. Your work is saved.' When they click 'Sharpen my idea' the panel shows a red 'That step failed' box with the same paused text and a 'Try again' button. admin.categories_and_colours: The admin chart 'Study types found (AI-derived from abstracts)' uses the same shape and colour pairs as the user app: Trial blue circle, Cohort / case-control orange square, Cross-sectional green triangle, Qualitative / mixed methods amber diamond, Systematic / scoping review pink star, Other design green cross, Not reported grey ring. Shape plus text label means colour is never the only cue. The segments sum to the paper counts users reported on each server: 115 (4101), 127 (4102), 111 (4103), 96 (4104), 118 (4105), 44 (4106), 73 (4107). Two things worth noting: 'Other design' is the largest or second largest bucket on 4101, 4102, 4103 and 4105, so the main category tells the admin little. Two greens (triangle for cross-sectional, cross for other design) look similar at a glance. Long labels are cut off ('Qualitative / mixed met...', 'Systematic / scoping r...'). In 'Quality signals', blue circle means verified and red triangle means unverified. 'What appraisals were based on' uses blue for full text and amber for abstract only, so blue and amber carry different meanings in two adjacent panels; the labels keep this readable. I did not use the paper table or map for study and article type filtering; that was outside the admin task.
admin.validity_assessment: Counts match what users said on all 7 servers, with the exceptions below. Users and projects: 2 on each of 4101 to 4106 (admin plus one user), 3 on 4107 (admin, chaos and the second account someone.else@example.org). Projects: 1 on each of 4101 to 4106, all 'Finished'. 4107 has 2 projects: 1 finished and 1 at 'Furthest step 1 of 9' (someone.else), AI calls 0, which matches 'idea only, nothing run'. Funnel: 1 project at every step on the single-project servers; on 4107 Idea shows 2 and all later steps 1. Appraised papers (full text plus abstract only): 10 (4101), 11 (4102), 15 (4103), 14 (4104), 14 (4105), 13 (4106), 10 (4107), matching what each user said, except that 4101 said 4 full text and the dashboard shows 4 full text and 6 abstract only, which also matches. Quotes: the verified and unverified counts match the users. 4102 shows 117 and 12, 4103 shows 139 and 14, 4104 shows 14 unverified (1 rejected plus 13 left), 4101 shows 11 (about 10 rejected plus 1 left). Summary batches: 12 calls on 4101 (12/12 batches), 10 on 4104 (10 of 10), 4 on 4106 (4 batches). Scoping calls fit the 2 to 4 questions answered. Server errors 0% on every server. This fits the users' reports of no failed network requests, since 4xx responses are not counted as errors. Mismatches: (1) the AI call total after the pause test (tile 56, breakdowns 58, account row 4), see the first finding; (2) the dashboard shows no client-side errors and stays green although every user hit 'removeChild'; (3) 4105 has ranking 29 calls and synthesis 6 calls against 15 to 19 and 3 to 5 elsewhere; (4) rejections and undecided quotes are not shown, and 0x stale on 4107 cannot be checked against the reopened step 2. AI off/on: when off, the dashboard went amber, the user saw 'AI is paused by the administrator. Your work is saved.' (plain, not faked, not mock text), the server answered 503 and nothing was spent. The headline AI call tile stayed at 54 while off. After turning AI on again, the user continued after a page reload (56 on the tile). Privacy: no ideas, papers, notes, passwords or keys are shown. The key is shown only as '••••RWBq' with 'From the server environment'. Emails appear in the Accounts table and audit log, never in a URL (the URL stays /admin). I did not paste, test, replace or clear a key, and did not change the spend limit.

admin.narrative: I started on the 4101 landing page, logged in and looked for the dashboard. The Account and settings menu has an 'Admin dashboard' link, so that took one click. The top of the dashboard answers in about three seconds: 'Is Athena healthy?' with a green verdict and six tiles. I then went through each server and checked the numbers against what each user told me. They matched closely: user and project counts, the funnel, appraised papers, verified and unverified quotes, and study-type totals that add up to the paper counts each user reported. The places where I could not confirm a claim were rejected quotes, the reopened step on 4107, and extra ranking and synthesis calls on 4105. What bothered me most was the green 'Everything is healthy' on every server even though every user had hit the same browser error, because the dashboard cannot see browser errors. For the pause test on 4102 I turned AI off through a clear dialog and the top of the page turned amber. In the second browser the new user saw a calm banner, but the scoping panel then showed a red 'That step failed', a spinner and a useless 'Try again', and nothing moved on. The headline call count stayed at 54, which was good, but after I turned AI back on the tile said 56 while the charts and tables said 58 and the user's row said 4. Two paused attempts are counted in some places and not in others. The user needed a reload to continue. Privacy looked fine: counts only, a masked key, no ideas or papers, no emails in URLs, though full emails show in Accounts and the audit log actor.
